summary: Observations of the slow and silent passage at low altitude of 7 dark objects keeping a constant course: probable observations of a group of balloons moving in the direction of the wind.
description: GEIPAN continues to publish its entire archive on its public website www.geipan.fr. These publications include older cases, originally classified as A, B, C, or D, which are now being re-examined to refine the conclusions. Thanks to new technical resources (software) and the investigative experience gained over the years, this re-examination sometimes leads to new observations or even a change in classification. This observation, previously classified as D and named LE HAVRE (76) 2006, is one of a group of cases recently re-examined. On the afternoon of December 15, 2006, several witnesses in the city observed the slow and silent passage of seven brown objects at low altitude in the sky. The objects were described as being shaped like "hockey pucks" and maintaining a constant course. The hypothesis of passive objects carried by the wind, such as balloons, is plausible and the most likely explanation for the nature of the UFOs observed by witnesses (see the investigation report). The witness statements collected by the Gendarmerie, as well as their subsequent calculations, such as the direction of movement and speed of the UFOs and their maintenance of a constant course, are consistent with the measured wind direction. The color and especially the shape (as described by T1 and T2, shaped like a hockey puck) are not common for balloons, but this cannot invalidate the hypothesis. There are many different types of balloons, with very diverse shapes and colors. It should be noted that these UFOs were seen during the day, from an urban area, at low altitude (T2 indicates that they passed behind buildings), and for at least 10 minutes. It is highly probable that these UFOs were seen by other people without being perceived as strange, which would further support the balloon hypothesis. The evidence is consistent, with witnesses providing fairly detailed accounts of their observations, police officers recording the sightings, and a location map. However, the lack of angular measurements of the UFOs' sizes and movement is regrettable, as this would have facilitated calculations of their dimensions, distances, and possible speeds. Consequently, GEIPAN classifies the case as B: probable observation of a group of balloons moving in the wind.

On October 31, 2006, a motorist spotted a peculiar luminous phenomenon behind the clouds. An intermittent white light appeared to be moving slowly. That evening, an electric string of lights placed on a viaduct was illuminated. The police investigation determined that the witness, misled by the poor weather conditions, mistook this luminous display for a UFO.

summary: Observation of the passage of 2 military aircraft in maneuver
description: On September 26, 2006, in Landrecies, at approximately 9:30 PM, a witness watching television with their children suddenly heard a loud noise that shook the house and saw a light outside. They went outside and saw two lights approaching the house with a very loud, low rumble. Two orange orbs hovered above the house for a few seconds before moving away. Further on, the two orbs separated before disappearing into the distance. Throughout the observation, the low rumble was continuous, increasing significantly at the moment of separation. The phenomenon was accompanied by a gas that irritated the eyes and throat. The witness's spouse, who was not home when the phenomenon occurred, returned about ten minutes later and noticed the lingering irritating odor. Within a radius of about twenty kilometers, other witnesses heard and/or saw part of the phenomenon. The following day, witnesses observed a whitish substance on the ground in several locations directly beneath the presumed path of the phenomenon. This substance disappeared in sunlight. Analysis of samples taken from this substance by the Forensic Science Institute revealed no traces of kerosene, and nothing linked these deposits (likely a natural phenomenon caused by humidity) to the observed phenomenon. The investigation concluded that the witnesses had observed two Mirage fighter jets on approach to Cambrai in a configuration that required them to fly very low and very slowly.

summary: Observation of the rapid movement of two luminous spheres.
description: On June 18, 2006, at 10:33 PM (the time recorded by one of the witnesses' phones), two fishermen on the beach observed a peculiar phenomenon. Two luminous, slightly translucent, yellow-orange spheres moved at high speed. These spheres disappeared into the mist as they headed north. No other accounts of this phenomenon have been collected. The investigation, launched late in 2008, failed to yield conclusive information (such as radar data, which is only archived for two months). The initial investigations were inconclusive.

summary: Daytime observation from a point above the Iroise bridge.
description: On September 13, 2006, at 10:00 AM, a witness, along with others, observed a stationary luminous phenomenon above the Iroise Bridge for three to four minutes. This phenomenon was circular and disappeared following an upward trajectory in the sky. The witness's account remains very brief. Given the response from the maritime authorities, there is a strong probability that the witness saw a small aircraft (a white, single-engine civilian plane was indeed in the area at the time indicated).

summary: Curious image in photograph: probably a plant seed.
description: While emptying his camera's memory card, an amateur astronomer noticed an intriguing image on the last photo. He hadn't seen or heard anything unusual when the photograph was taken 10 days earlier. After analyzing the sent image, he concluded it was likely a plant seed that had passed close to the lens when the photo was taken.

summary: Observation of an unidentified stain on a photograph.
description: On September 1, 2006, a witness took photos of a film shoot taking place in his village. Upon examining the photos, despite having made no visual observations, he noticed an unfamiliar stain on one of them. He contacted the air transport police to file a report. A meticulous investigation was conducted by the gendarmerie, which ruled out the hypothesis of a meteorological phenomenon but revealed an unknown radar trace composed of three points recorded by the primary radar in Nice around the same time as the photograph was taken, showing a rapid acceleration of the presumed object. This lead was dismissed (see report) in favor of, subsequently, the possibility of a commercial aircraft, reference 7637, passing by. Furthermore, the company responsible for maintaining the clock in the bell tower stated that they were being bothered by pigeons, which, by landing on the hands, disrupted the clock's operation. There is therefore a colony of pigeons in the bell tower, the presence of which is confirmed by the photograph in which numerous pigeons are clearly visible on the cornice below the clock. The hypothesis of a bird passing through the frame of the photograph is therefore perfectly plausible, the blur The observed phenomenon could be caused by wing flapping. The available evidence does not allow us to definitively conclude either hypothesis; the passage of a pigeon, despite some uncertainties, seems to be the more likely explanation than that of commercial flight reference 7637. Regardless of the hypothesis adopted, a conventional explanation can be provided for this case, which should therefore be classified as B e.

summary: Observation of two luminous spheres above the ocean.
description: Recent report (June 4, 2008) of a previous observation. In August 2006 (perhaps the 12th), during the "Night of the Stars" around 11:30 PM, a witness observed a luminous phenomenon from the Saint-Jean-de-Monts pier. Two faint spheres moved low above the ocean. The observation lasted 30 seconds before the spheres became very bright and disappeared in a fraction of a second. No other reports concerning this phenomenon have been collected. This observation is similar to that of sky lanterns, but we lack details and information.

summary: Observation of the silent movement of a luminous phenomenon in the sky: probable observation of the passage of a Thai lantern.
description: On June 20, 2006, at 11:30 PM, a witness in the Fontainebleau forest was intrigued by the passage of a luminous, creamy-white disc across the sky. Its trajectory was straight, from west to east, with a steady speed. No unusual noise was heard during the two- to three-minute observation. This somewhat strange phenomenon of a luminous point moving across the sky, following the wind direction, suggested a Thai lantern, likely licked during a solstice festival. The oval shape and cream color (the observer was in complete darkness, so all light appeared white) were consistent with this hypothesis. The GEIPAN (French Astronomical Society) classified this case as "B": probable observation of a Thai lantern.

summary: Observation of the rectilinear and silent movement of a black object in the sky: lack of information.
description: Recent report of a previous observation: A witness observed, during April 2006 at 10:00 AM (the exact date is not specified, the date given here is arbitrary), the silent and straight movement of a black object in the sky. The speed was constant, and the object disappeared below the horizon. The witness compared the object to an "oil barrel" or a "black cabin." The relatively low altitude, the black barrel shape, and the slow movement, possibly driven by the wind, suggest a thermal (solar) balloon. As the date is unknown, this hypothesis cannot be confirmed. GEIPAN classifies this case as "C": lack of information.
